title: Branches, commits, pull requests and merges
summary: Learn why Showmob changes stay reviewable and what a merge actually changes.

blocks.title: Git keeps the work reversible; GitHub makes the review visible
blocks.body: A branch is an isolated line of changes. A commit is a named snapshot. A pull request compares the branch with main so tests, previews and review comments can happen before main changes. A merge records the accepted branch history on main.

blocks.heading: 3. A clean Showmob PR
items: State the user-visible intent and follow-ups in the PR body.
Run content validation, npm run build and git diff --check.
Use the Vercel preview to inspect the exact branch output.
Address useful review findings in the same branch.
Merge only when the head commit and passing checks are the ones reviewed.
